_notice: Demo data. Safety protocols are standard pre-arrival guidance for a hackathon prototype and MUST be reviewed by medical/fire/police authorities before any real-world use.

fire.label: Fire

resources.note: if anyone is hurt, burned or has inhaled smoke
only if chemicals / industrial site is involved

triage_questions: Is anyone inside or trapped, or hurt?
What is burning - a building, a vehicle, vegetation, an electrical fitting?
Is the fire spreading, or are there gas cylinders or chemicals nearby?

default: Get everyone out of the building right now and stay out - do not go back inside for belongings.
Stay low under the smoke and keep doors closed behind you to slow the fire.
Do not use the lift. Use the stairs.
If your clothes catch fire: stop, drop to the ground, and roll.

flood.label: Flood

resources.note: when people are stranded by deep or moving water
if anyone is hurt or unwell

triage_questions: How deep is the water right now - ankle, knee, waist, or higher?
Is the water rising, and is anyone stranded or unable to leave?
Are there children, elderly or people who cannot walk with you?

default: Move to higher ground or an upper floor now - do not wait for the water to rise further.
Do not walk, swim or drive through moving floodwater. Even shallow fast water can knock you down.
If you can do it safely, switch off the electricity at the main switch and stay away from fallen wires.

road_accident.label: Road Accident

resources.note: if anyone is trapped in a vehicle
only when vehicles block the road and nobody is trapped

triage_questions: How many people are hurt, and is anyone unconscious or not breathing?
Is anyone trapped inside a vehicle?
Is there fire, smoke or fuel leaking?

default: Do not move the injured person unless there is fire or immediate danger.
Switch on your hazard lights and stay well away from moving traffic.
If someone is bleeding heavily, press firmly on the wound with a clean cloth and keep pressing.
cpr: Lay the person flat on their back on a firm surface.
Put the heel of one hand in the centre of the chest, other hand on top.
Push hard and fast - about two pushes every second - at least five centimetres deep, and let the chest come back up each time.
Keep going without stopping until the ambulance crew takes over.

road_blockage.label: Road Blockage / Obstruction

resources.note: only for landslide debris / tree removal with people at risk

triage_questions: What is blocking the road, and is it fully blocked or one lane?
Is anyone hurt or trapped, or are there live wires involved?

default: Stay clear of the obstruction and warn approaching drivers if it is safe to do so.
Keep away from any fallen wires - treat them as live.

medical.label: Medical Emergency
triage_questions: Is the person awake and breathing normally?
How old is the patient, and what exactly happened?
Is there severe bleeding, chest pain, or any known condition or medication?

default: Keep the person still and comfortable. Do not give food or drink.
Loosen tight clothing and stay with them.
If they become unconscious or stop breathing, tell me right away.
cpr: Lay the person flat on their back on a firm surface.
Put the heel of one hand in the centre of the chest, other hand on top.
Push hard and fast - about two pushes every second - at least five centimetres deep, and let the chest come back up each time.
Keep going without stopping until the ambulance crew takes over. I will stay on the line with you.
bleeding: Press firmly on the wound with a clean cloth or your hand and do not lift it to check.
If blood soaks through, add more cloth on top and keep pressing.
Keep the injured part raised if you can.
choking: If they cannot cough, speak or breathe, stand behind them and give five firm back blows between the shoulder blades.
Then five abdominal thrusts: fist above the navel, pull sharply inward and upward.
Alternate back blows and thrusts until it clears or they become unconscious.
childbirth: Help the mother lie down or sit comfortably with knees bent, and stay calm.
Do not pull on the baby. Support the head as it comes and keep the baby warm and skin to skin once born.
Do not cut the cord. The ambulance crew will do that.

industrial_chemical.label: Industrial / Chemical Accident
triage_questions: What do you smell or see - gas, smoke, liquid spill?
Is anyone having trouble breathing, feeling dizzy, or collapsed?
Is it a factory or a home, and is anyone still inside?

default: Move away from the area right now - go upwind and uphill if you can.
Do not switch any electrical switches on or off, do not use a lighter or flame, and do not start a vehicle nearby.
Cover your nose and mouth with a wet cloth and warn people around you to move away.

building_collapse.label: Building Collapse

resources.note: if fire, gas or dust hazard

triage_questions: Are people trapped under or inside the rubble, and how many?
Can you hear anyone calling out or tapping?
Is there gas, fire, or a further collapse risk?

default: Stay out of the damaged structure and keep everyone away - more of it may fall.
Do not try to dig out trapped people with heavy lifting unless a person is in immediate danger.
If you can hear someone, keep talking to them and tell them help is coming.

natural_disaster.label: Natural Disaster
triage_questions: What is happening where you are, and is anyone hurt or trapped?
Are you in a safe place right now?

default: Move to an open, safe area away from buildings, trees and power lines if you can.
During an earthquake: drop, cover your head, and hold on until the shaking stops.

crime.label: Crime / Violence in Progress

resources.note: only if someone is hurt - keep it staged until police clear the scene

triage_questions: Are you safe right now, and can you speak freely?
Are the people involved still there, and is there a weapon?
Is anyone hurt?

default: If you can get away safely, do so. If not, get somewhere you can lock or block the door and stay quiet.
Silence your phone ringer, keep out of sight, and do not confront anyone.
Stay on the line with me if it is safe. If it is not safe to talk, I will stay on and listen.

utility_failure.label: Utility Failure

resources.note: only if people are at risk
if there is a fire or gas explosion risk

triage_questions: What has failed - a live wire down, a gas smell, or a burst water pipe?
Is anyone in contact with it or close to it, and is there fire or sparking?

default: Stay at least ten metres away from any fallen wire and treat it as live. Do not touch anything in contact with it.
If you smell gas, leave the area, do not use switches or flames, and do not use any phone close to the leak.
Keep other people away from the area.

missing_person.label: Missing Person / Search & Rescue

resources.note: only for large or remote searches

triage_questions: Who is missing - age, what they were wearing?
Where and when were they last seen, and could they be in danger from water, heat, or traffic?

default: Stay where you last saw them if you can, and keep your phone free for us to call back.
Do not search into dangerous areas like deep water or busy roads alone.

animal_rescue.label: Animal-related Emergency

resources.note: crowd or traffic control if needed

triage_questions: What animal is it, and is it behaving aggressively or is it injured?
Is anyone in danger or hurt?

default: Keep well away from the animal and do not try to corner it or feed it.
Move children and pets indoors and keep doors closed.

public_disturbance.label: Public Disturbance
triage_questions: How large is the crowd, and is it turning violent?
Is anyone hurt or being crushed?

default: Move away from the crowd towards an open exit or side street and keep your hands free.
If you are caught in a crush, keep your arms up in front of your chest and move with the crowd, not against it.

other.label: Other Emergency
triage_questions: Can you tell me what is happening and whether anyone is in danger?

default: Move to a safe place away from any danger and stay on the line with me.
